The importance of the 2026 election is obvious. A dictatorial president subverting the constitution to gain more power for himself while Congress stands by in thrall, subservient to his political movement. November may be our last chance to stand and defend our democracy and our elections.
Pitch in $35 -- right now -- to fuel our efforts to inform eligible voters, get them registered, get their ballot cast, and make every vote count >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=061826_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

subject: I will shut down Pete Hegseth’s incompetent reign of terror.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Let me be frank about something. I am a Black man born and raised in rural Louisiana. As a third generation farmer, my son and I work the same Delta land that my granddad worked as a sharecropper—except now we own it.
What I am trying to say is: I can smell racist BS from miles away. And right now, Pete Hegseth’s Defense Department stinks to high heaven.
Pete Hegseth is playing favorites and passing over qualified Black and female servicemembers for promotions, and targeting them for demotion and dismissal—while also promoting inexperienced MAGA loyalists.
Nearly 60 percent of the senior officers fired by Hegseth are female or Black. Women and racial minorities in our military have been denied promotions, baselessly fired or dismissed, or have been pushed out of the ranks at alarming and unprecedented rates.
Rewarding loyalty to MAGA above the experience, expertise, and exemplary service of the men and women who have dedicated their lives to our country is both despicable and dangerous.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
This isn’t about DEI, racial equity, or even just basic human decency: Pete Hegseth’s unsteady, bigoted, and dangerous leadership of the Department of Defense is putting every single one of us at risk.
Hegseth has unraveled the merit-based system that kept our military strong for generations. He’s turning our military into a MAGA loyalty clown show.
I pledge to you: When I am elected to the United States Senate, I will make it my personal mission to shut this foolishness down and get back to putting experienced personnel in the positions that matter most .
I am Jamie Davis, a third-generation family farmer running to defeat MAGA extremism in this wide open US Senate seat in Louisiana. Together we can make history, flip this seat, and reclaim the US Senate for Democrats. Will you make a donation of $15, $25 or any amount to help me and my team pull off an upset victory this midterm election? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
HELP ELECT A REAL WORKING-CLASS CHAMPION TO THE SENATE! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jamie]
Thank you. Your support means more than you know.
Jamie Davis
Democrat for US Senate
Louisiana

body:
Peter, we must prepare our workers for the changing economy.
Hello Peter,We are living through a period of rapid technological change, and while innovation can bring great benefits, it also brings real disruptions to our workforce.**Recently, in just one single month, six companies closed their facilities in Wisconsin, costing nearly 1,000 of our neighbors their jobs. Across our country, thousands of workers are facing layoffs due to the impact of automation and AI.** This is a crisis that we cannot ignore. If we do not act, our workforce and our communities will be left behind.As a former senior leader in the Department of Workforce Development, I know that we must proactively prepare our workforce for the jobs of tomorrow.**Instead of waiting for layoffs to happen, we must:**
* Expand pre-apprenticeship and technical training programs to help workers transition into high-skill, family-supporting careers.
* Partner with our world-class Wisconsin technical colleges and the private sector to align training with real, available jobs.
* Create incentives for businesses to upskill their current workers rather than replacing them.

When I was at the Department of Workforce Development, I led an effort to quickly review, approve, and contract a public-private grant to help hundreds of Wisconsinites enter pre-apprenticeship training for construction trades. That's the kind of speed and decisiveness we need to protect our workers.We can protect Wisconsin jobs and make our state a leader in the modern economy.**Please consider supporting our campaign today so we can bring this critical, forward-looking leadership to Madison.**[**[PROTECT WISCONSIN JOBS ➔]**](https://willmartinforltgovernor.cmail20.com/t/j-l-ydkhwdk-hkjudtlhit-r/)Thank you for your partnership.Warmly,Will Martin

name: The Democratic National Committee
subject: It’s not time to panic… yet
body:
---
Derek — our end-of-quarter deadline is in just a couple of weeks. Once it passes, we’ll be required to report how much we’ve raised in Q2, and _everyone_ will be looking at that number. **The truth is that we _need_ to report a strong fundraising total.** Not just to show that we have strong support behind us, but because we absolutely have to hit our fundraising goals to ensure that Democrats have the resources that they need to run winning campaigns this year. Right now, we’re pacing to fall short of our goal, **_but we’re not panicking yet.**_ We’re going to need a massive influx of grassroots contributions to finish strong, Derek. And if every person receiving this email chipped in $7, _we’d blow our end-of-quarter goal out of the water._ But the unfortunate truth is that most people won’t even open this email, let alone give. Not just to show that we have strong support behind us, but because we absolutely have to hit our fundraising goals to ensure that Democrats have the resources that they need to run winning campaigns this year. Right now, we’re pacing to fall short of our goal, but we’re not panicking yet. We’re going to need a massive influx of grassroots contributions to finish strong, Derek. And if every person receiving this email chipped in $7, we’d blow our end-of-quarter goal out of the water. But the unfortunate truth is that most people won’t even open this email, let alone give. So since you’ve made it this far, we have to ask: If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly. | | | ** | | | | | | | ** Thank you for your support, The Democrats If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support.

We need a Senator who has ****already answered the 3 A.M. call**** —and brought everyone home.

body:
| Roughly 2.1 million Americans identify as transgender.
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you'd like to unsubscribe,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=1&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11950?t=2&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)Peter, Roughly 2.1 million Americans identify as transgender. They are our neighbors, siblings, friends, parents, and spouses. They work hard to support themselves and their families. Some have also chosen to serve our great nation in the military; in local, state, and federal government; and in other leadership positions. On day one of his second term, President Trump signed an executive order to **remove all trans people from military service.** Trans adults nationwide have lost access to medical treatment or even had treatments canceled because hospitals and clinics have been forced to roll back gender-affirming care under Trump. **It’s clear that transgender Americans have become a scapegoat for the GOP. We must stand up for our neighbors and speak out against these discriminatory policies._[Sign on now to show your support for trans rights in the United States!](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13752?source=LOC_EM_PET_2026.06.18_OG-Trans-Rights_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=3&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)_** | [SIGN ON NOW →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/13752?source=LOC_EM_PET_2026.06.18_OG-Trans-Rights_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T0&t=4&akid=2528%2E259176%2EhVWg8m)

**We _cannot_ let Donald Trump and his cronies get away with these hateful and unjust policies.**
**[_Will you pledge to stand with Blue Amp Action and defend the rights of transgender Americans? name: Barlow For Wyo
subject: Barlow For Wyoming Newsletter
body:
Special Forum Edition
| | | | | | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_0)
---
| **Welcome to the Barlow for Wyoming Newsletter. Your hub for latest news, information and upcoming events.**
---
|
---
| | |
---
| Hi Friends,When I decided to run for Governor, I told my campaign team to look for opportunities where I could join other gubernatorial candidates to discuss the issues facing Wyoming and dive in deeper than just top-line messaging. I am so thankful to the many organizations across the state that have stepped up to host forums and debates. Unfortunately, we can't attend all of them. But I am trying to make as many as feasible and ensure I cover as broad a range of topics as possible.I have appreciated each of these conversations. The questions have been thoughtful, practical, and rooted in the real work happening across Wyoming every day. So far, we have talked about our legacy and future extractive energy industries, healthcare, education, taxes, local government, economic development, families, and the future of our communities.These forums are important because they give Wyoming voters the chance to hear directly from candidates and think through the kind of leadership our state needs.For Kelly and me, they have also been a reminder of why we are in this race: to listen, work hard, and stay focused on Wyoming solutions for Wyoming problems. I am not running against anyone, I am running for Wyoming which hopefully is evident in how I show up at these events.
* After tonight's Wyoming Republican Party debate, I will have met other candidates at 7 forums with at least 4 more planned. Below is a list of past and upcoming forums including the names of the host organizations.
* May 11, Petroleum Association of Wyoming (Casper)
* June 4, Wyoming Mining Association (Gillette)
* June 5, Wyoming Association of Municipalities (Laramie)
* June 5, Greater Cheyenne Chamber of Commerce (Cheyenne) -- forum recording below
* June 9, Wyoming Family Conservative Candidate Forum presented by the Wyoming Family Alliance (Cheyenne) -- forum recording below
* June 12, Wyoming Healthcare Policy Summit presented by the Wyoming Medical Society, Wyoming Hospital Association, Wyoming Nurses Association, and Wyoming Primary Care Association (Laramie) -- forum recording below
* June 18 at 7:30pm, Wyoming Republican Party (Dubois) -- watch it live or recorded later [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y805InM6ArI](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_1)
* June 23, Gubernatorial Candidate Agriculture Forum Breakfast presented by the Wyoming Farm Bureau Federation, Wyoming Stock Growers Association, and Wyoming Wool Growers Association (Casper)
* July 22, League of Women Voters, WyoFile, and Wyoming Public Radio Gubernoatorial Forum (Casper)
* July 30, The 2026 WCSP Gubernatorial Forum presented by Wyoming Community Service Providers, Natrona Collective Health Trust, Wyoming Governor’s Council on Developmental Disabilities, Wyoming Independent Living, and Child Development Center
* August 6, The 2026 Gubernatorial Debate presented by Wyoming PBS, Wyoming Public Media, and Cowboy State Daily

Not all forums were streamed or recorded, but several were. I encourage you to watch and share with your friends, especially those who you are reminding to vote in the upcoming primary. Watch the campaign social media sites and newsletters for reminders and links to upcoming events.See you on the trail!\- Eric
---
| | [ SUPPORT ERIC! ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_2)
---
|
---
| **FORUM POSTS FROM FACEBOOK**
---
| **WYOMING HEALTHCARE POLICY SUMMIT** I appreciated being asked to join the forum at the Wyoming Healthcare Policy Summit in Laramie. I’ve watched many in that were in the room make improvements and serve Wyoming citizens for years, even as things have gotten tougher, but there is still a lot of work to do. Let's keep going.
---
| | [ Watch the Healthcare Forum Replay ](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01KVEXANVE9Z36AJ738N05YM2Y_3)
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **WYOMING FAMILY ALLIANCE** I participated in the Wyoming Family Alliance forum in Cheyenne, and it was a fruitful discussion about what Wyoming families need. Kelly and I believe Wyoming families are the foundation of everything we are fighting for. Parents deserve a real voice in their children’s education. Communities deserve local control. And every child in Wyoming deserves the opportunity to get a meaningful education, raise a family, and build a life right here at home. We are pro-life, and we back that up with support for maternal health, community-based care, and resources for women and children across Wyoming.

## Oil Flows as Iran Deal Takes Effect
The U.S. [lifted its naval blockade](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAUhE-DOyz-FrMFRRp3mzalxZrH-kXYWICNNqePnCukHmlmvu_rMT0cRtxen24FW0OaNmglQq2Qp4QxxNRKTk_clpR8qRnAI0yCCU2Zpvw-eYfxPanO2wAgQHZg-WC40dII3S3WaBWeg_Sz5zczD-CN4lIpp81dQQDZob3amOZ3zjgTqldqvknp5MwVY9wNRDHwWFPuvxNudYEQ3-mE3M9p7aJdat0LkR9EjESMrbV-fpaL4sqJGCOeQI_duwqFiBGz22hzmdZ8rDs9CvXgIi01O6w0BbqkvB4_RIxdtn5vGCMWfZ14rQ7j32j9l6nTit8AAAD__4hnfmg) of Iran on Thursday, and oil tankers began moving through the Strait of Hormuz for the first time in 110 days, as the deal to end the war officially took effect. ## Robin Hood's Legendary Tree Dies
The [Major Oak in Sherwood Forest](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOke7tjFQuPibdPnbK5GDl7B3DotsKxFvfyKvcPVI8803X7fpFjjx9vgfnuTrItNG75KoVsqTcFqSvEuWO2-rSCw1E0WmSYN2CpzCcYqB0zHZNvqFSJNpyWM_4ODMoF27-uhcXLAzTsM8UOxCIDM4u3T9ON5xNi37sw0cjggI2l6snTtjgpnRAmDoGwsUuUq-fAtvdaUlHfKifJnl2Sa_1rqXxvxr9LXR151kT3RGjb6GbWbaqpLwo87p6mOiThUVmYpCpQHUQSEXhRoAu35ss4_7m1Pi4k724xk4fVj1Twe9vP4NAAD__xTpeKM), the 1,200-year-old tree that legend says sheltered Robin Hood inside its hollow trunk, is believed to have died after failing to produce leaves this spring. The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds said centuries of visitors [compacted the soil](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd1iAHWwXFJFWlrbIdqsprWd4xG-EIQImnvz9yPmFqa_u1Tn347bcgALF-z_Y0VSflohHCVgr5iVR8CEdJaeV4paSKzUjOsJFCaW50FxOiwMKr6VvnPGICrsGjRxGOepuVLrZzDpKDWIaJg9y7eQA4NCOdhW9t0L7tSFzrgktJymkUH3b9_bSddBZ2QshYWC9QEc15fYzUawb-vBKT8ytTXsTzFbro7DuytTM1HwcR7uXeGZMzRg5fDE17ynii6n5jhEzBKZmiJYwVv5246ccP-U4Fe4QHMfvB-ZaeIGzB5lfr-ry_y_8abJxj4NCoKJPtPsOFN4o9Vf_PY36CQAA__96T4Us) around the massive oak until it was as hard as concrete, strangling the root system and cutting off water and nutrients. The tree had been fenced off since the 1970s, but the damage was already deep. Metal bracing, concrete fills, and structural props meant to save the tree likely made things worse, preventing it from aging naturally. Recent heatwaves and drought compounded the decline. The oak will remain standing as a wildlife habitat and monument, and saplings from the tree have been planted around the world. A Hugh Jackman film, _The Death of Robin Hood_ , opens Friday. ## Supreme Court Sides with Texas Man
The U.S. Supreme Court [ruled unanimously on Thursday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGyozAMBdCvMZ0Y2_hBKCi2oXvbbsnIIIL3gZ2x5JD8_Q75hW3UaOaeO_fP9_SNYQ_x_hsPGuS1pinSyTuJUJ6Kp5yTT4KvwCFuqbCkuOLPZLVtQbdg-mnBsL8nVy2D10tvKhpMdzO3ttO2q7ahX13XmC_C1vXOz7r3XafRzx5bcq7zVRiuMN2a3hjdOFc33n0tfeublXqjG1JO0xIk5Vo2Enohr_s7PSnXczqqfdhEHqyaX8qOyo7nedY_jHI9lR194RCJWdnxYpQd9XXMTdmRyyPTQTCnkgU4LMRwBtkA4cPAgRHOLQHjmyEIQ0wCCHMOB8GaMhyYw9-CEaEwZQZJsOGT4F7iJVZ5WB5n2PfAbaecvh8Y9k9r-b-tn4P9FwAA___WlpVR) that the government cannot strip a Texas man of his guns because he uses marijuana. The decision in _U.S. v. Hemani_ favored Ali Danial Hemani, charged under a 1968 law after FBI agents [found a handgun and marijuana](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD0TnCAYhH-NdjiAiFJQpLG7tCkdPl71zSE4gOfdv89cyrQpd3ZmZ5_n12N5GAwYt5_mAF3fa1oi3CVArZCXy0LOyaZq3lgw7ukqNcXVPBdOuSRUEqYWbzB8FtF6balXrAXNxolNcqR8bHc9gBiHwYMRSspxGDll1FnB5eAnJenUov6OUckUY7QXouutGLyStl9BMdpDIyh4rCl3dYcKb1PW8EkvyJ1LRxv0XutZmv5Hw-eGz_d9d9G6L8W3b_h8poAVXWn4XK4zwwHEpSvXfzOxxj0LOUzG35eJhlwFciFuNyFA3IBkKDWjq5gi2a5I0h0hlx1JdtFwKVXP2qz9eWMIWOTYCLodBsPfn_X_7L40_xMAAP__9NmSgQ) at his Texas home. He faced no other charges and wasn't accused of being armed while high. Writing for the court, [Justice Neil Gorsuch said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL0O3CAQhJ8Gd1gsJjYuKNK4u7QpLTCLjYLhxM_57u0jn5QnSLVajebTzPx-rA_tg4_7L32iqm-X1ohXCVgr5rUZzDmZVPXbFx-P1EpN0ek_K2d8pGykMK9W-_BZRWeVYXaGDhVMEuQ4MT51h9qsQ0AjQcIouZA4owQEdJMYGHDXeXXD2AgzABuE6Acjfth5NIPDGdiARDC0vqbc1wMrvnVx4ZNemPstnV1QR63PQoafhC-EL9d19dFs1l23TPhy97mPrj5FHaiPFfO_j_CltGfGE-mWWq70y6ebLkiDvqjNbaetYC50b5Ee7TZT4y1GwhfBBgmzIHzpsrLPy4fgyzgRwfZT-_DNV_9v1ZfifwMAAP__m2GOeQ) the government can't treat everyone who regularly uses marijuana as "categorically violent and dangerous." The narrow ruling leaves the underlying ban intact and marked a loss for the Trump administration, which defended it. The case drew unusual allies. The ACLU and the National Rifle Association backed Hemani, while gun-control group Everytown and the Justice Department argued that habitual drug users pose a danger that justifies the ban. The Public Utility Commission was set to vote yesterday on an ERCOT plan to [study data-center hookups in groups](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCnwQ4DiAoFxTZ2d9stDcivkmFgAr-j8_Yb5xVuc5qTfDk5_37mHxtiSNtf-wSD15rnBGeNgAhlPhyUkl1Ge4Ua0p6Pijmt9jELJgbKBsr17G2In1k23jjmNW_A8FFxNYxMjM1uBrUq6P3qe67A9tqOzjvdA_OsV9LLJpgbYwPXnLNOyrZzsvd6cN0KmrMOiGTgA-bS4g4Il61r_OQ3lHbJzyaaHfFVSfeHiImI6TzP9uHwuksiptsmYmJ3cEXE9AVozPlRKYZtR0i0HBEq9RYtXSAhlEpxhw-NIQE9XnTJKcGCFMqSkW4leCKmphj_OkOMoQ4jkWx72hC_k_B3R76N-B8AAP__iaWI6g), or "batches," rather than one at a time. ERCOT says its old system, built for 40 to 50 large projects, was swamped by 225 requests last year, about 70% of them data centers. Supporters say the change protects grid reliability, while some residents worry about the strain on power, water, and neighborhoods. The overhaul follows a [directive this month](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S4yAQhJ9GylDxIyMREFzibC-9UDWCwaIOMy4Yeb1vf-W9R9i4u77q_v58bB-QS66333BHz69EW8XPXpAZ23bu2BrtxPDKPdeDzs5UE_zdtNRWSCuU2yLk8rXNY_S7jE6N6NWyqtUuUi_j4a2BOZl0kWCNc5D0uhoDaokurHNUlzH7N0xa5ZSSZp4ns8-X6OxuEjolDQ6zxJiZ2sQHMr6gp_JFT2xToPtY_MH86IP5NejroK83ek7fpelGz0Ff33cGfX1Q5_8ptkpNwL4Ts4i5YeAuHmcQUKPAFogFk-hHxhLFm1S7SI3uIgKDCFgZm8g1NejczsBnQxGocx-bj4_PXErudhlmebtDLt8b-Wdmn17_CwAA__808ZH8) from Gov.
